prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove chosen proteins, through PROTACs and through the molecular basis of cereblon-directed glue degraders.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B029 alone, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical principle, event-driven and catalytic induced proximity, in which a small molecule removes a protein rather than blocking it. The round-1 exchange did not weaken this. Six of eight configurations now centre on it, and every supporter, including those who disagree with me on the third name, describes the mechanism (E3 recruitment, ternary-complex formation, cereblon as the thalidomide target) as independently confirmed. I weigh that scientific agreement above the vote count. The founding PROTAC concept and 2001 proof of principle belong to Crews and Deshaies, and Handa's identification of cereblon is the mechanistic discovery that turned an old drug into a rational glue platform. A citation that names the principle and both entry routes is accurate about how the field arose, and it does not claim that the two strands were one discovery.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the therapeutic claim remains prospective, and a committee that prefers clinical vindication could reasonably wait. Attribution is the most serious weakness. The three-name cap leaves out Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs drug-like, and also Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim, each with a credible claim. The citation also joins two lineages that were discovered separately, and a critic could say that this is done to fit the cap. I accept all three objections as real costs. I judge them smaller than the cost of a prize that omits either the heterobifunctional concept or the cereblon mechanism.

responses.point: Chabes and Somfai prefer Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a citation limited to heterobifunctional PROTACs, on the ground that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made the concept a drug-like chemical tool.
responses.response: This is the sharpest disagreement within the B029 group and I have weighed it again. A PROTAC-only citation is cleaner historically, and Ciulli's contribution is chemically concrete. But the question the chair raised is whether one citation can cover both strands honestly. I think Handa makes that possible, because cereblon explains thalidomide, lenalidomide and the whole glue field, and a prize silent on it would read as incomplete to anyone working in the area. Ciulli's work is a refinement and enabling step within the PROTAC concept. Handa's is a separate mechanistic discovery. That is why I would still drop Ciulli, with real reluctance, rather than Handa. If the committee settles on a PROTAC-only scope, I would accept Ciulli in the third place.

responses.point: Brzezinski names Crews, Ciulli and Handa in round 1 and treats Ciulli as a live contender over Deshaies, while ranking B056 (long-range protein electron transfer) first.
responses.response: I do not think Deshaies can be removed. The 2001 PROTAC paper came from the Crews and Deshaies groups together, and Deshaies' later work on the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery supplied the biochemical frame for E3-directed degradation. A trio without him would credit the optimisation of a concept but not its origin. On B056, I still regard it as rigorous and well confirmed, and I would not oppose it as a prize. My concern is its narrower reach beyond protein electron-transfer physics, together with its place in the Marcus lineage already recognised in 1992. I also note that you described its clinical counterpart for B029 as slightly early. I agree that this is a caution, but not a reason to prefer a more mature field.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, moved from a Ciulli-containing trio to Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and he stresses that approval of a degrader drug is an open question and a real caution.
responses.response: I share your reasoning on Handa, and your move confirms that the combined citation reads as the more complete one. On approval, I would not make a regulatory event the test. The Committee has recognised principles whose validity rested on mechanistic confirmation and wide independent adoption, and B029 has both, with many degraders in clinical trials. I would treat approval as supporting evidence and not as a precondition. Your own alternative, B058, shows how strongly a clear physical mechanism pulls, but the same standard of mechanistic clarity is met here, in the biochemistry of ternary complexes.

responses.point: Sparr proposes B055 (Hyman and Brangwynne) with B006 (Cullis alone) as a two-part prize, argues from physical-chemical substance rather than support counts, and lists B029 as an alternative.
responses.response: I respect that you argue from substance, and the founding observation of liquid-like P granules is cleanly attributed to Hyman and Brangwynne. My hesitation about B055 remains that the central question, which cellular assemblies are truly equilibrium phase-separated liquids, is still contested, and a prize could seem to endorse an overextended claim. For B006 I agree the chemistry of ionizable lipids is real, but a single-name award to Cullis leaves out Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Langer and Anderson in a crowded lineage, and the 2023 Medicine award on mRNA overlaps the application. That is why I keep B006 only as an alternative. If B029 is not accepted as a single prize, I would look at a second part, but I would want it justified independently of B029.

responses.point: Zou prefers base editing (B047) credited to Liu alone, acknowledges the overlap with CRISPR-Cas9 (Chemistry 2020), and notes thin long-term safety and off-target data.
responses.response: Narrowing to Liu alone makes the attribution cleaner, but it does not remove the other objections you list. The adenine editor involved real protein engineering, and I regard B047 as a credible alternative, which is why it is on my list. My difficulty is that a prize for base editing following the 2020 prize is likely to be read as a second award for the same revolution, and Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida all have contributions that a single name would erase. Your own first alternative is B029, which suggests the comparison turns on distinctness and maturity, and I think B029 is stronger on both.

uncertainties: Whether the third laureate should be Handa or Ciulli, and whether a PROTAC-only citation would be historically cleaner than a combined PROTAC and glue citation.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug should delay recognition, which I cannot resolve from the files and treat as a matter of judgment.
Whether Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim are left out unfairly, and whether any two-part prize that separated PROTACs from glues would be fairer than one combined citation under the three-person limit.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My postdoc mentors, Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey, are not credited on any shortlisted ballot. My field overlaps with Emma Sparr's on self-assembly, but this is not a personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate, and I have no tie to any credited name in B029.
